denomProfiles/charismatic-renewal/taglin: Pentecostal-style renewal of the Spirit within Catholic, Anglican and Protestant churches.
denomProfiles/charismatic-renewal/coreDo: Baptism in (or "release of") the Holy Spirit as a renewal of baptismal grace.
All the gifts of 1 Corinthians 12, including tongues and prophecy, are for today.
Participants generally keep the doctrine and sacraments of their own churches.
Tongues are welcomed but usually not required as initial evidence.
denomProfiles/charismatic-renewal/focuse: Personal encounter with the Holy Spirit.
Renewal and unity of the churches.
denomProfiles/charismatic-renewal/practi: Prayer groups with tongues, prophecy and prayer for healing.
"Life in the Spirit" seminars (Catholic) leading to prayer for Spirit baptism.
denomProfiles/charismatic-renewal/influe: Many independent churches grew from charismatic fellowships.
Charismatic songs became widespread in many denominations.
The Vatican service for Catholic Charismatic Renewal (2019).
denomProfiles/charismatic-renewal/keyFig: Episcopal rector whose 1960 announcement launched the renewal.
Healing evangelist with a wide cross-church audience.
Cardinal and patron of Catholic Charismatic Renewal.
Leader in the Catholic renewal after the 1967 Duquesne Weekend.
denomProfiles/charismatic-renewal/member: Pew Research Center (2011) estimate of charismatic Christians worldwide in non-Pentecostal churches.
denomProfiles/charismatic-renewal/inIndi: Catholic Charismatic Renewal is especially strong in Kerala, where the Divine Retreat Centre at Muringoor (founded 1987 by the Vincentians) draws very large crowds, and charismatic prayer groups are common in Catholic parishes across south India.
denomProfiles/neo-charismatic/tagline: Independent, indigenous and network churches of the global Spirit-renewal movement.
denomProfiles/neo-charismatic/coreDoctri: The present-day work of the Holy Spirit in signs, wonders and spiritual gifts.
Spirit empowerment for all believers, usually without a requirement of tongues as initial evidence.
Evangelical teaching on salvation, often with strong emphasis on healing and deliverance.
In many networks, the restoration of apostolic and prophetic ministries.
denomProfiles/neo-charismatic/practices/: Leadership by founders or apostolic networks rather than denominations.
Healing crusades, prayer mountains and all-night prayer.
denomProfiles/neo-charismatic/keyFigures: Founder of the Vineyard and of "power evangelism".
Coined "Third Wave" and promoted the New Apostolic Reformation.
Founder of an African church counted in this category.
denomProfiles/neo-charismatic/members/no: Estimate of neocharismatics (independents and Third Wave) by David Barrett and Todd Johnson in the New International Dictionary of Pentecostal and Charismatic Movements (2002).
denomProfiles/neo-charismatic/inIndia: Thousands of independent Pentecostal and charismatic churches and ministries operate across India, from house-church networks in the north to large Tamil ministries such as Jesus Calls (founded 1972 in Chennai).
denomProfiles/church-of-god-in-christ/ta: The largest historically Black Pentecostal church, born of holiness preaching and Azusa Street.
denomProfiles/church-of-god-in-christ/co: Trinitarian evangelical faith with the Bible as the inspired, infallible Word of God.
Holiness: sanctification as a real work of grace producing a separated, holy life.
Baptism in the Holy Spirit, evidenced by speaking in tongues, as an experience after conversion.
Divine healing through prayer and anointing, alongside the use of medicine.
denomProfiles/church-of-god-in-christ/fo: Holiness of life and personal testimony.
Evangelism and church planting in Black communities in the United States and abroad.
A strong Women's Department, founded in 1911 under Lizzie Robinson.
Civil rights and community uplift, symbolised by Mason Temple in Memphis.
denomProfiles/church-of-god-in-christ/pr: Three ordinances: water baptism by immersion, the Lord's Supper and foot washing.
Exuberant worship with gospel choirs, shouting and the "tarrying" service for Spirit baptism.
The annual Holy Convocation, held for most of its history in Memphis.
Government by bishops under a Presiding Bishop and a General Board.
Women serve as evangelists, missionaries and church mothers but are not ordained as pastors or bishops.
denomProfiles/church-of-god-in-christ/in: Many white ministers who formed the Assemblies of God in 1914 had held COGIC credentials.
COGIC musicians such as Mattie Moss Clark, the Hawkins family and Andraé Crouch shaped modern gospel.
Martin Luther King Jr. gave his last speech, "I've Been to the Mountaintop", at Mason Temple on 3 April 1968.
denomProfiles/church-of-god-in-christ/ke: Co-founder and first Chief Apostle and Senior Bishop (d. 1961).
Co-founder who rejected tongues as initial evidence and led the Church of Christ (Holiness).
First head of the Women's Department (from 1911).
Leader of the Azusa Street Mission where Mason received Spirit baptism.
denomProfiles/church-of-god-in-christ/me: US membership reported by the church to the Yearbook of American and Canadian Churches (2012 edition); the church itself often cites about 6.5 million.
denomProfiles/church-of-god-cleveland/ta: One of the oldest Pentecostal denominations, rooted in Appalachian holiness revival.
denomProfiles/church-of-god-cleveland/co: A Declaration of Faith (1948) affirming the Trinity, the inspiration of Scripture and salvation by grace through faith.
Three works of grace in the Wesleyan-holiness pattern: justification, sanctification and Spirit baptism.
Baptism in the Holy Spirit with speaking in tongues as the initial evidence.
Divine healing provided for in the atonement.
The premillennial second coming of Christ.
denomProfiles/church-of-god-cleveland/fo: Holiness of life, set out in its "Practical Commitments".
World missions: the church reports congregations in more than 180 countries.
Education through Lee University (founded 1918) and the Pentecostal Theological Seminary.
denomProfiles/church-of-god-cleveland/pr: Water baptism by immersion, the Lord's Supper and foot washing as ordinances.
Revival-style worship with altar calls, prayer for healing and tongues.
A biennial International General Assembly that sets doctrine and polity.
Centralised government under a General Overseer and appointed state and regional overseers.
Women may be ordained ministers (from 2010) but not bishops or members of the governing councils.
denomProfiles/church-of-god-cleveland/in: Formed by A. J. Tomlinson's followers after his removal as General Overseer in 1923.
Church of God (Full Gospel) in India
Robert F. Cook's Kerala mission affiliated with the Cleveland church in 1936.
Its missions built large churches across Latin America and the Caribbean.
denomProfiles/church-of-god-cleveland/ke: Baptist minister who founded the Christian Union in 1886.
General Overseer 1909–1923 who led the church into Pentecostalism.
Evangelist who carried Azusa Street Pentecostalism to the south-eastern United States.
denomProfiles/church-of-god-cleveland/in: The Church of God (Full Gospel) in India grew from the work of the American missionary Robert F. Cook in Kerala, which joined the Cleveland church in 1936; it is strongest in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, with a separate Dalit-led section in Kerala.
denomProfiles/foursquare-church/tagline: Aimee Semple McPherson's church of Jesus as Saviour, Baptiser, Healer and Coming King.
denomProfiles/foursquare-church/coreDoct: The "Foursquare Gospel": Jesus Christ as Saviour, Baptiser with the Holy Spirit, Healer and Coming King (from Ezekiel's four-faced vision).
A Declaration of Faith written by McPherson in the 1920s, evangelical and Trinitarian.
Baptism in the Holy Spirit, normally with speaking in tongues, as an experience after conversion.
Divine healing in answer to believing prayer.
The imminent, premillennial return of Christ.
denomProfiles/foursquare-church/focuses/: Evangelism through mass meetings, radio and media.
Church planting, with tens of thousands of congregations reported worldwide.
Social relief: Angelus Temple's commissary fed many thousands during the Depression.
Training leaders through LIFE Bible College (1923, now Life Pacific University).
denomProfiles/foursquare-church/practice: Believer's baptism by immersion and the Lord's Supper.
Contemporary Pentecostal worship with prayer for healing.
A centralised corporation in which local church property is held by the denomination.
Women ordained as pastors since the founding, by a woman founder.
denomProfiles/foursquare-church/influenc: Chuck Smith trained at LIFE Bible College and pastored Foursquare churches before Calvary Chapel.
McPherson's KFSG (1924) was among the first radio stations owned by a church.
Jack Hayford and The Church on the Way
Hayford's Van Nuys congregation and worship songs such as "Majesty" reached far beyond the denomination.
denomProfiles/foursquare-church/keyFigur: Founder, evangelist and pastor of Angelus Temple (d. 1944).
Her son, president of the church 1944–1988.
Pastor, hymn-writer and president of the church 2004–2009.
denomProfiles/apostolic-church/tagline: Welsh-born Pentecostal church that governs through living apostles and prophets.
denomProfiles/apostolic-church/coreDoctr: Eleven Tenets, evangelical and Trinitarian, including the inspiration of Scripture.
The "divine appointment" of present-day apostles and prophets, with evangelists, pastors and teachers (Ephesians 4:11).
Baptism in the Holy Spirit with signs following.
Divine healing and the gifts of the Spirit.
The second coming of Christ and the eternal state.
denomProfiles/apostolic-church/focuses/0: Church government under the guidance of recognised apostles.
denomProfiles/apostolic-church/focuses/1: Directive prophecy, historically used even in appointments to office.
denomProfiles/apostolic-church/focuses/2: Overseas mission, especially in Nigeria, Ghana and elsewhere in Africa.
denomProfiles/apostolic-church/focuses/3: Training through its colleges and the annual convention at Penygroes.
denomProfiles/apostolic-church/practices: Believer's baptism by immersion and regular communion.
Recognition and ordination of apostles and prophets.
The August International Convention at Penygroes, Carmarthenshire, held since the 1910s.
Tithing as a principle of church support.
denomProfiles/apostolic-church/influence: Formed in 1941 from the Faith Tabernacle and Apostolic Church movement led by Joseph Ayo Babalola.
Grew from the work of the Apostolic Church missionary James McKeown, separating in 1953 and later becoming one of Ghana's largest churches.
Its doctrine of present-day apostles anticipated the British House Church movement.
denomProfiles/apostolic-church/keyFigure: Founder and first President, recognised as apostle.
Missionary to the Gold Coast from 1937.
Nigerian revivalist associated with the church in the 1930s.
denomProfiles/elim-pentecostal/tagline: Major British Pentecostal denomination founded by the healing evangelist George Jeffreys.
denomProfiles/elim-pentecostal/coreDoctr: Evangelical, Trinitarian Foundational Truths, with the Bible as the inspired Word of God.
Salvation by grace through faith in Christ's atoning death.
Baptism in the Holy Spirit with the gifts of the Spirit.
Divine healing as part of the gospel.
denomProfiles/elim-pentecostal/focuses/0: Evangelism and healing campaigns, historically on a mass scale.
denomProfiles/elim-pentecostal/focuses/1: Church planting in Britain and Ireland.
denomProfiles/elim-pentecostal/focuses/2: Overseas mission, notably in southern Africa.
denomProfiles/elim-pentecostal/focuses/3: Ministerial training at Regents Theological College.
denomProfiles/elim-pentecostal/practices: Believer's baptism by immersion and the Lord's Supper.
Contemporary Pentecostal worship and prayer for healing.
A centralised Conference with a General Superintendent and church property held by the movement.
Women may serve in all levels of ministry.
denomProfiles/elim-pentecostal/influence: Founded by Jeffreys after he left Elim in 1940 over central control.
Elim's London church became one of Britain's largest congregations.
Elim fed leaders and worship styles into wider British evangelicalism.
denomProfiles/elim-pentecostal/keyFigure: Founder and evangelist whose campaigns filled the Royal Albert Hall.
His brother, also a healing evangelist.
Secretary-General who organised Elim's centralised structure.
